title: Our place in the Milky Way
summary: A barred spiral seen from inside: the arms are fitted to parallaxes of young massive stars, the Sun sits 8.2 kpc from the centre between two arms, and the nearest stars, the Oort cloud and the heliosphere bring the scale down to the solar system.

concepts.label: Galaxy
concepts.description: The Milky Way, a barred spiral about 30 kpc across; structure inferred from inside its disc.

children.label: Spiral arm
children.description: A log-periodic spiral fitted to maser parallaxes: R_kink, β_kink, pitch angles, width.

facts.text: The Milky Way is very likely a four-arm spiral with some extra arm segments and spurs.

children.label: Galactic bar and bulge
children.description: Long bar half-length 5.0 ± 0.2 kpc at 28–33° to the Sun–centre line; boxy/peanut bulge.

children.label: Galactic centre
children.description: Sgr A*, a 4.3 million solar-mass black hole.

children.label: Nebula and star cluster
children.description: Real objects at measured distances: H II regions, open and globular clusters, remnants.

concepts.label: Star
concepts.description: A star within 100 light years: HYG (names, types) and Gaia DR3 (parallaxes, colours).

children.label: Spectral type
children.description: O B A F G K M (and white and brown dwarfs): temperature, hence colour.

children.label: Exoplanet host
children.description: A star with known planets (NASA Exoplanet Archive).

concepts.label: Distance
concepts.description: How far, and how it was measured: trigonometric parallax (Gaia, VLBI masers), stellar orbits (S2 around Sgr A*), expansion.

children.label: Parallax
children.description: d = 1/π: Gaia DR3 for stars, VLBI for masers in the arms.

concepts.label: Solar system's outer reaches
concepts.description: Kuiper belt, scattered disc, heliosphere (crossed by both Voyagers), and the hypothesised Oort cloud.

children.label: Oort cloud
children.description: Hypothesised shell of icy bodies, inferred from long-period comets, never observed.

children.label: Heliopause
children.description: Where the solar wind meets the interstellar medium, ~120 AU.
